verdict: Ingersoll Rand grew revenue 6% to $2.06B — and reported profit nearly tripled to $670M, because about $355M of settlement recoveries from the old ILC Dover deal landed in the quarter.

segments.name: Industrial Technologies & Services
segments.note: Compressors, vacuum and blower systems, power tools and lifting equipment — orders jumped 25% on long-cycle projects.

segments.name: Precision & Science Technologies
segments.note: Precision liquid, gas and powder handling for life sciences, aerospace and defense — life-sciences orders grew double digits.

opex.name: Selling & administrative
opex.note: Selling the equipment and running the company.

opex.name: Amortization of intangible assets
opex.note: Spreading the cost of past acquisitions over time — a non-cash charge.

opex.name: ILC Dover settlements & other operating income
opex.note: Money back, not a cost: settlements with insurers and others over the ILC Dover transaction, plus IEEPA tariff refunds, booked as operating income.

otherDetail: Interest expense of $63M, partly offset by $5M of other income.

takeaways.title: A settlement did the heavy lifting
takeaways.text: GAAP net income of $671M includes about $355M of operating gains, mostly ILC Dover settlement recoveries. Adjusted net income — the underlying run-rate — was $415M, up 24%.

takeaways.title: Orders are booming
takeaways.text: Orders rose 21% to $2.35B (18% organic), including a roughly $195M engineered-to-order infrastructure order; both segments grew.

takeaways.title: Cash flow doubled
takeaways.text: Free cash flow was $623M versus $326M a year ago, helped by $162.5M of settlement cash collected in the quarter.

oneTimers: Other operating income of $355M: Ingersoll Rand reached settlements with insurers and other parties over the ILC Dover transaction totaling about $425M of gross recoveries ($25M collected in Q2, $162.5M in Q3, the rest expected in Q4), alongside IEEPA tariff refunds. Excluding tariff refunds, adjusted EPS was $1.01 instead of $1.07.
footerNote: Net income of $671M is before $2M attributable to noncontrolling interests; net income attributable to Ingersoll Rand was $670M, the basis for the $1.73 EPS. Figures are rounded to $M; selling & administrative absorbs a $1M rounding difference so the lines add exactly.
